title: Oklahoma City: Henry Bridges' drive-in quartet and Bill Powell
summary: Tenor player Henry Bridges lets him take up tips and teaches him songs; singer Bill Powell then takes him to Seminole.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: So we finally got a guy to take us back to Oklahoma City, my sister and I. So we went to Oklahoma City. And I run into Henry Bridges. Have you ever heard of him?

Yeah, a tenor player. Well, actually, I got to know him. And he was working with a quartet out there at some drive-in place where the people would drive in and they'd request numbers. He'd play a number for them, and then, you know, you'd take the hat around and they'd go and throw tips in it and so forth. So he said, "Why don't you come and take up the money?" and so forth. But I really wanted to play. So I'd say, "Well, look, how about letting me play, too?" He said, "Well, that's all right. When we ain't got nothin' to do, I'll teach you what I know." So he taught me a lot of songs that I had never heard of.

But anyway, we did that for a while, and I got so I could eat by taking up the change, and the guys would chip in and give me something to have so I could go to a restaurant, after we got back in town, and eat, and so forth

and so on.
So a guy came in town named Bill Powell -- he was a singer and dancer.

Yeah. Bill Powell. And he came in, and Henry told him about me, that I was a trumpet player. So he asked me would I want to go down to Seminole, Oklahoma. So I said, 'Why not? I ain't workin' here. I ain't makin' no money anyway.'
Now, where were you living at this time?
Oh, I was living in Oklahoma City at some place that I had rented from a lady for three dollars a week. A horrible place...
Just a place to be, just to sleep.
